aligned_items.summary: independent Rust driver topology under drivers/block/rnull/ with switchable Kbuild integration
configfs-controlled device creation, power on/off lifecycle, and configfs root subsystem
queue_mode=1 reject and queue_mode=0 downgrade to blk-mq behavior match the C baseline
shared_tags powered-on queue-count update behavior now matches the C baseline runtime

unaligned_items.summary: manual configfs AttributeList wiring remains in the abstraction layer instead of using the mature configfs_attrs! path
Rust candidate adds broad main.c-core functionality absent from both official Rust references
full frozen target runtime validation is blocked by the C-baseline mbps runtime gap

functional_differences.summary: The implementation intentionally exceeds official Rust rnull feature scope because the frozen C target includes configfs, memory-backed I/O, queue updates, shared tags, badblocks, poll queues, and mbps.
Only zoned support and fault injection remain excluded, and both were frozen explicitly in phase 0 rather than silently dropped.
C baseline and Rust candidate align on most runtime-visible paths, but the frozen mbps target lacks credible C-baseline closure under the current harness, so full equivalence cannot be claimed.

engineering_differences.summary: The candidate front-ports new public abstractions into rust/kernel/configfs.rs, rust/kernel/time/hrtimer.rs, rust/kernel/block/badblocks.rs, and rust/kernel/block/mq/* instead of keeping logic inside the driver.
The candidate uses a controller plus runtime/backing object model, whereas both official references keep a much smaller fixed-function structure.
The candidate's memory-backed storage and throttling internals differ structurally from the C radix-tree and queue-stop model.

old_tree_constraints.summary: The lower-bound official reference predates the directory split and configfs support; compare must account for drivers/block/rnull.rs as the true initial shape.
configfs_attrs! could not be used for this baseline-tree rnull shape, forcing manual attribute wiring inside rust/kernel/configfs.rs.
Generic blk-mq and hrtimer helper bridges remain necessary on this tree.

workflow_defects.summary: The guest runner originally reused global shell loop variables and produced a false infinite lifecycle loop.
The guest I/O tool originally missed delayed writeback errors because fsync and close failures were not audited.
The early helper audit still reflected planned helpers rather than the actual retained helper set until refreshed.

tool_failures.summary: No clear blind-first tool failure was identified in the final compare; the remaining blockers are old-tree constraints or runtime closure gaps.

answers.scope_expansion_or_shrink: The implementation expands far beyond official Rust rnull, but that expansion is intentional and required by the frozen C main.c core + configfs target. No silent shrink was identified beyond the explicit zoned and fault-injection exclusions.
answers.delta_vs_initial_official: Compared with bc5b..., the candidate adds configfs, runtime configurability, memory-backed I/O, queue updates, badblocks, poll queues, timer completion, and shared tag handling.
answers.delta_vs_mature_official: Compared with 63c37d..., the candidate still exceeds the mature official feature surface substantially, but it also depends on unreviewed local abstractions and manual configfs wiring that the mature tree avoids.
answers.version_evolution: The move from single-file fixed-function rnull to directory topology plus configfs is normal version evolution.
answers.process_problems: Harness bugs, stale helper-audit wording, and the initial shared_tags update restriction were workflow defects uncovered by this rerun.
answers.real_tool_failures: No distinct tool failure remains after fixes; the unresolved issue is a runtime gap on the C baseline mbps target.
